Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

begin verb

also start, begin to, start to, commence, make a start

classical

Hor. Ep. 1.2.41: sapere audē, incipe
Ov. F. 1.149: quārē novus incipit annus

incipiō, incipere, incēpī, inceptum

verb, third conjugation

begin, start

With an infinitive, with an object, or alone, and things begin too (incipit annus). For the past say coepī: Cicero uses incipiō only in the present system (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • coepī, coepisse, coeptum — began, have begun

    verb, defective (perfect forms only) · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.2.40: dīmidium factī, quī coepit, habet; Phaedr. 1.13.5: deinde sīc coepit loquī

    The past of “begin”; with a passive infinitive it is passive too: ars habērī coepta (Liv. 39.6.9).

  • incohō (inchoō), incohāre, incohāvī, incohātum — begin, start (a piece of work)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Mart. 13.36.2: inchoat atque eadem fīnit olīva dapēs

    Of starting something that is to be finished: a building, a book, a meal.

  • initium facere — make a start

    also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 14.36: facere initium cōnflīgendī (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.1.5: initium capit ā flūmine Rhodanō, of a region that begins at a river

Examples

  • dīmidium factī, quī coepit, habet; sapere audē, incipe

    well begun is half done: dare to be wise, and beginHor. Ep. 1.2.40–41

  • dīc, age, frīgoribus quārē novus incipit annus, quī melius per vēr incipiendus erat?

    Come, tell me: why does the new year begin in the cold, when it would better have been begun in spring?Ov. F. 1.149–150

  • animadvertuntque ea, quae domī fīunt, cūriōsius incipiuntque commentārī aliquid et discere

    and they watch what goes on at home more keenly, and begin to make things up and to learnCic. Fin. 5.42

  • dum haec Taurus, intereā puer vēnerat et aula dēferbuerat tempusque esse coeperat edendī et tacendī

    while Taurus was saying this, the boy had come in, the pot had stopped boiling, and it was time to eat and stop talkingGell. 17.8.17

See also end, end, begin to boil, continue, stop.
